ranking.strengths: Bold cream gear, copper holder, and dark edge give the gap and separate hardware strong phone-size silhouettes. Flat, faceted finish is furthest from glossy neon plastic. The assembled view leaves both gaps visible and places the holder on an intact arc.
ranking.flaws: The broad U appears to grip roughly half the ring, so it could not pass through the approximately 60-degree gap. It reads more like a flat gear plate than a tube, and the heavy black outline could dominate when sprites shrink. The tiny bolts will vanish at game size.

ranking.strengths: Chunky ivory ring and matte tan holder are easy to separate, tint, and build from bevelled primitives. Rounded ends and few details should survive downscaling.
ranking.flaws: Soft clay-like forms lack a crisp mechanical identity. In the assembly the ring's gap sits at the holder, with two isolated cuffs on the open ends instead of the pictured continuous U wrapping an intact tube. The U also spans far more arc than the gap, so the release action is not credible. The attached second ring is closed.

ranking.strengths: Precise bevels, finished ring ends, and brass-and-ivory contrast make a polished mechanical presentation. Gear teeth and standalone gap are easy to identify.
ranking.flaws: In the assembly the U sits over the gap, so no intact tube is visibly captured; its long arc could not slip through a 60-degree opening. Gold teeth and end caps are part of the ring and complicate clean ten-colour tinting. Screws, inset panels, and thin trim become noise at phone size. The attached second ring is closed.

ranking.strengths: Simple repeating teeth, pale base, and bevelled U are straightforward to model and recolour. The standalone gap has a generous opening.
ranking.flaws: Icy glow, translucent-looking edges, and shiny white surfaces drift toward the forbidden glossy neon-plastic look. Ring and holder share nearly the same value, merging at small size. The assembled U covers the ring gap and spans much more than 60 degrees, preventing the intended release. The attached second ring is closed.

build_notes: Keep concept 4's graphic cream ring, copper holder, and restrained dark edge, but fix the mechanism before modeling. Use a C-shaped mesh from a bevelled annular strip or curve, about 300 degrees of ring with a true 60-degree empty sector; make radial band width about 14% of outer radius and add 11-13 broad, evenly spaced outer teeth, with no tooth bridging the gap. Round the two cut ends with a bevel about 10% of band width. Give the ring a shallow convex tube face and broad highlights so it reads as a tube in orthographic top-down view, not a solid plate. Use a neutral off-white, moderately rough ring material for per-ring colour tint; keep the holder as a separate matte copper or dark bronze material with small, dull metal fasteners. Build the stem and mount from bevelled boxes; simplify bolts to two readable discs or omit them at final sprite size. Make the functional clamp a short saddle at one angular position, with inner and outer lips wrapping the tube's radial cross-section and a visible dark groove between clamp and ring. Keep its total angular contact footprint under about 45-50 degrees, including both lips and clearance, so the 60-degree gap can rotate fully beneath it and let the ring separate. The larger U silhouette may remain as a decorative recessed yoke behind this short saddle, but must not touch the tube outside that footprint. Render orthographically with broad soft light, restrained bevel highlights, and a thin dark contact shadow; test at actual phone sprite size on charcoal before finalizing.
